planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into consistently moist, strongly acidic, poorly drained soil in full sun to partial shade; littleleaf titi is a coastal-plain wetland specialist and struggles in dry or neutral-to-alkaline sites.

directions: Cyrilla parvifolia is a finer-textured, more strongly evergreen counterpart to the widespread swamp cyrilla (Cyrilla racemiflora), distinguished by smaller, leathery leaves and a more compact, rounded form; it occupies depressional wetlands, pocosin margins, and wet pine flatwoods from the Florida Panhandle into southern Georgia. Like its larger relative, it produces slender racemes of small, fragrant white flowers in early summer that draw heavy native bee and honeybee activity, making stands of it a valued regional honey source. Site it in a boggy corner, rain garden, or pond margin with reliably wet, acidic soil, since it has almost no tolerance for dry or well-drained conditions. Because true seed-grown plants are uncommon in the trade, most nursery stock is produced from softwood cuttings taken from known wild or cultivated populations.
sources: Flora of the Southeastern United States (FSUS), UNC Herbarium

common_name: Soleil Golden Wax Myrtle (Yellow-Leaved Southern Wax Myrtle)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in well-drained, acidic to neutral soil in full sun; foliage color is brightest with maximum sun exposure and tends toward green in heavy shade.

directions: 'Soleil' is a golden-foliaged selection of southern wax myrtle first isolated as a single yellow-leaved seedling from a breeding population in Raleigh, North Carolina, and since propagated by cuttings to hold its color true. Unlike the species' typical gray-green leaves, 'Soleil' emerges bright gold and holds a warm chartreuse-yellow tone through the growing season, giving it real value as a color accent or contrast planting against darker evergreens in a native-plant border. It retains the aromatic foliage, adaptability to poor sandy or salty soils, and wildlife-supporting berries (on female plants) of the species, so pollinators and berry-eating birds still benefit even where it is grown chiefly for its foliage color. Give it full sun and reasonably drained soil; the gold color washes out toward plain green in shadier or excessively wet sites.
sources: US Plant Patent PP18,731 — Myrica plant named 'Soleil'
North Carolina State University Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

common_name: Whit XXIX Wax Myrtle (Cold-Hardy Deer-Resistant Selection)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in well-drained, acidic to neutral soil in full sun to partial shade; this selection tolerates colder winters than typical southern wax myrtle stock.

directions: 'Whit XXIX' is a named selection of southern wax myrtle bred by Oklahoma nurseryman and plant breeder Carl Whitcomb for improved cold tolerance and dense, upright evergreen structure, and it has reportedly withstood temperatures down to about -18 degrees Fahrenheit in trials — well beyond the hardiness expected of typical wax myrtle. Its habit is notably denser and more upright than seed-grown wax myrtle, with most new growth concentrated on a strong second summer flush, giving a tighter screen with less pruning. The aromatic evergreen foliage is reported to be less palatable to white-tailed deer than ordinary wax myrtle, a meaningful advantage in areas with heavy browse pressure. Use it as a hedge or evergreen screen in regions where standard wax myrtle risks winter dieback, while retaining the same wildlife and pollinator value as the species.
sources: US Plant Patent PP34,687 — Southern wax myrtle or bayberry plant named 'Whit XXIX' (Lacebark Inc.)

common_name: Bayside Bonito Wax Myrtle (JBG 1000 Heat-Tolerant Selection)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in well-drained to moist, acidic soil in full sun; this selection was bred and tested specifically for Gulf Coast heat and humidity.

directions: Marketed under the trade name Bayside Bonito, 'JBG 1000' originated as a seedling selection near Houston, Texas, chosen for standout vigor and heat and humidity tolerance under the intense growing conditions of the upper Gulf Coast. Its light, vibrant green, strongly aromatic foliage stays dense and clean through summer heat spells that can stress ordinary wax myrtle stock, making it a reliable choice for screening in the hottest parts of its native range. Like the species, it fixes nitrogen through root associations with Frankia bacteria and tolerates poor sandy soils, salt spray, and periodic wet spells once established. Grow it as an evergreen hedge, mixed-border anchor, or wildlife screen where summer heat and humidity are the limiting factors for other broadleaf evergreens.
sources: US Plant Patent PP36,234 — Wax myrtle plant named 'JBG 1000'
Proven Winners ColorChoice — Bayside Bonito Southern Wax Myrtle

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in well-drained, acidic to neutral soil in full sun to partial shade; naturally compact habit needs little or no shearing to stay dense.

directions: 'BTC-1' arose from an open-pollinated cross between two unnamed wax myrtle selections in Augusta, Georgia, and was chosen for its unusually compact, globular, freely branching habit with much shorter internodes than typical seed-grown plants. The dense, dark-green aromatic foliage fills in tightly from the ground up without the leggy, open base common to standard wax myrtle, so it holds a neat rounded form with minimal pruning. This makes it a practical choice for foundation plantings, mixed shrub borders, or smaller residential lots where full-sized wax myrtle would quickly outgrow its space. It keeps the species' tolerance for poor sandy soils, salt spray, and drought, along with the berries that feed overwintering songbirds on female plants.
sources: US Plant Patent PP19,789 — Wax myrtle plant named 'BTC-1'
